Part (b): Prove that eigenvectors belonging to distinct eigenvalues are independent.

Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.

\[\det(A-\lambda I)=(13-\lambda)(15-\lambda)=0.\]
Final answer: \(\lambda=13,15\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
For a shortest relation \(\sum c_i\mathbf v_i=0\), applying \(A-\lambda_nI\) produces a shorter relation \(\sum_{i<n}c_i(\lambda_i-\lambda_n)\mathbf v_i=0\), forcing all coefficients to vanish.
Final answer: Distinct-eigenvalue eigenvectors are independent.

questions.prompt:
Part (a): Find an eigenvector of \(A=\operatorname{diag}(14,16)\) for \(\lambda=14\).
Part (b): Prove that the eigenvalues of a unitary matrix have modulus one.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[(A-14I)(x,y)^{\mathsf T}=(0,2y)^{\mathsf T}=0,\]
so \(y=0\) and \(x\) is free.
Final answer: One eigenvector is \((1,0)^{\mathsf T}\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
If \(U\mathbf v=\lambda\mathbf v\), norm preservation gives \(\|\mathbf v\|=\|U\mathbf v\|=|\lambda|\|\mathbf v\|\). Since \(\mathbf v\ne0\), \(|\lambda|=1\).
Final answer: Every unitary eigenvalue satisfies \(|\lambda|=1\).

questions.prompt:
Part (a): Calculate the eigenvalues of \(A=\begin{pmatrix}15&1\\0&17\end{pmatrix}\).
Part (b): Prove that a triangular matrix has its diagonal entries as eigenvalues.
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[\det(A-\lambda I)=(15-\lambda)(17-\lambda)=0.\]
Final answer: \(\lambda=15,17\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
For triangular \(A\), \(A-\lambda I\) is triangular, so
\[\det(A-\lambda I)=\prod_i(a_{ii}-\lambda).\]
Its roots are exactly the diagonal entries.
Final answer: The eigenvalues are \(a_{11},\ldots,a_{nn}\).
